title: What Made Your Thali Costlier in July: Onions, Oil, and Chicken Drive Kitchen Inflation
excerpt: Home-cooked vegetarian meals rose 4% and non-vegetarian meals 9% year-on-year as onion, oil, LPG, and chicken prices surged, a Crisil report finds.
body:
• The cost of a home-cooked vegetarian thali in India rose 4% year-on-year in July, while a non-vegetarian thali became 9% costlier, according to Crisil Intelligence's latest report.
  • Onion prices jumped 20% year-on-year and 23% month-on-month, driven by depleted rabi stocks damaged by unseasonal rain in Maharashtra.
  • Broiler chicken prices surged 14% as the protein accounts for nearly half the cost of a non-vegetarian meal.
  • Lower potato and tomato prices partially offset the increases, but vegetable oil and LPG rose 10-11% due to the West Asia conflict.

Your home-cooked thali got noticeably more expensive in July. The cost of a vegetarian thali rose 4 percent from a year ago, while a non-vegetarian thali became 9 percent costlier, driven by sharp increases in onion, vegetable oil, LPG, and chicken prices, according to Crisil Intelligence's monthly Roti Rice Rate (RRR) report released on Friday.

The report, which tracks the average cost of preparing a meal at home using prevailing input prices across north, south, east, and west India, paints a picture of persistent kitchen inflation that has squeezed household budgets for much of 2026.

Onions Lead the Price Surge

Onions were the single biggest driver of vegetarian thali inflation in July. Prices jumped 20 percent year-on-year and a staggering 23 percent month-on-month as higher-priced stored rabi stocks dominated the market.

The supply crunch traces back to March and April, when unseasonal rain and hailstorms in Maharashtra — India's largest onion-producing state — damaged the late-season rabi crop and stocks in storage. With kharif onion arrivals still weeks away, prices have remained stubbornly elevated.

"Lower potato and tomato prices partially offset the increases, but vegetable oil and LPG rose 10-11% due to the West Asia conflict."

Vegetable oil added to the pressure, rising 11 percent year-on-year, while LPG cylinder prices climbed 10 percent. Both increases stem from supply disruptions linked to the ongoing West Asia conflict between the United States and Iran, which has roiled global energy and commodity markets.

Chicken Prices Hit Non-Veg Meals Harder

The non-vegetarian thali bore an even heavier burden. Broiler chicken prices surged 14 percent year-on-year, and since chicken accounts for nearly half the cost of a non-vegetarian meal, the impact was amplified across the plate.

The chicken price spike reflects a tighter supply chain. Extreme summer heat earlier in the year increased bird mortality, reduced weight gain in poultry farms, and discouraged fresh chick placements — a supply squeeze that is still working its way through the market.

On a month-on-month basis, however, the non-vegetarian thali held steady in July compared to June, as broiler prices dipped an estimated 2 percent during the month on softening demand, offsetting higher costs of other ingredients.

Some Relief From Potatoes and Tomatoes

Not everything on the plate got more expensive. Potato prices fell 12 percent year-on-year after rabi production rose 2-3 percent on higher acreage. Tomato prices also declined 2 percent year-on-year, though the relief was modest.

On a monthly basis, the vegetarian thali still became 2 percent more expensive in July compared to June, as the sharp jump in onion prices and a 4 percent rise in potato prices on a month-on-month basis outweighed the marginal decline in tomatoes.

What It Means for Indian Households

The Crisil report underscores how geopolitics and weather have combined to squeeze Indian kitchen budgets. The West Asia conflict continues to push up energy-linked inputs like cooking oil and LPG, while erratic monsoon patterns and extreme heat have disrupted vegetable and poultry supply chains domestically.

For the Indian diaspora, the thali cost index serves as a useful barometer of food inflation back home. When families in India report that groceries are getting more expensive, the data backs them up — and the drivers, from geopolitical conflict to climate disruption, are forces that show no signs of easing in the near term.

Crisil's RRR index measures the cost of a standard thali that includes roti, rice, dal, vegetables (onion, tomato, potato), curd, and salad for the vegetarian version, with broiler chicken replacing dal in the non-vegetarian plate. It tracks prices of cereals, pulses, vegetables, broilers, edible oil, spices, and cooking gas across four regions of India.
nri_angle: The thali cost index is a useful barometer of food inflation for diaspora families tracking the cost of living back home in India.
